Order:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Mr. G. Bhasker Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Mujib Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of Habeas Corpus directing the respondents to produce the detenu i.e., Bokka Praveen S/o Prabhakar @ Cheralu, who is no detained in Central Prison,
Cherlapally, Medchal - Malkajgiri District before this Court to order for his release forthwith by declaring his detention vide proceedings C.No.289/WRC/CSB-XI/2023, dated 21.04.2023 passed by respondent No.3 and the consequential confirmation order passed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt.No.821 of General Administration (Special Law & Order) Department, dated 06.06.2023 as illegal.
3.

Mrs. Bokka Mallika, the wife of the detenu, filed the present writ petition challenging the detention order dated 21.04.2023 passed KL,J & PSS,J by respondent No.3 and the consequential order dated 06.06.2023 passed by respondent No.1.

The aforesaid detention order was passed by respondent No.3 under Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land-Grabbers,
Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders,
Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders,
Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'White Collar Offender' relying on the following five (05) crimes;
Crime No. Offences Allegations levelled Remarks 502/2022 of KUC PS Section - 420 IPC & Cheated on the pretext Bail granted (CC 889/2023) Section 25 (1A) of the of providing jobs and Arms Act,

sentences.text:
In the detention order, there is also reference with regard to the involvement of the detenu in the following three (03) more crimes:
 Crime No. Offences Remarks 77/2023 of KUC PS Sections - 447, 427, 386 & 506 r/w Bail granted (charge sheet filed) 34 IPC 82/2023 of KUC PS Sections - 447, 427, 386, 506, 290 & -do- (CC 903/2023) 323 r/w 34 IPC 86/2023 of KUC PS Sections - 447, 386 & 506 r/w 34 IPC -do- (CC 904/2023)
5.
The order of detention was approved by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt. No.823, General Administration (Special Law & Order) Department, dated 06.06.2023.
Therefore, the petitioner herein filed I.A. No.2 of 2023 to amend the prayer.
She has filed copy of the said G.O. Rt.
Considering the said facts, the said I.A. is also allowed.

6. Mr. G. Bhasker Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the detenu is nothing to do with the aforesaid crimes and the allegations leveled therein are cooked up and far away from truth.
The police have foisted the aforesaid crimes in the recent past against the detenu with an ill motive to invoke the P.D. Act.
Basing on the said crimes, respondent No.3 passed the detention order which is illegal.

Further, the alleged extracting money on the pretext of providing jobs were in relation to March, 2021, whereas all the aforesaid crimes except Crime No.502 of 2022 (which was registered KL,J & PSS,J on 29.12.2022), were registered in the month of February, 2023.
There are probabilities of acquittal in the said cases as there is no material to prove the allegations levelled against the detenu.
7. He would further submit that the detention order was passed without application of mind and subjective satisfaction.
Preventive detention of a person is an extreme measure resorted to by the State when ordinary criminal law is found not adequate to control his activities which cause disturbance to public order.
In the case on hand, there is no disturbance caused to public order and the alleged offences are between the individuals.
Thus, passing of order of detention by respondent No.3 and the consequential confirmation order passed by respondent No.1 is illegal and the same are liable to be set aside.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents would contend that the Detaining Authority having satisfied with the material available on record and considering the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed by the detenu,
passed the order of detention.

He would further submit that the detenu was involved in eight (08)
KL,J & PSS,J crimes.
The offences committed by the detenu are grave in nature.
The Detaining Authority considering that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in future, which would again certainly affect the public order, issued detention order.
There is no error in it.
9. Perusal of the record would reveal that in all the aforesaid five (05) crimes relied on by respondent No.3 - detaining authority, there is delay in lodging complaints.
The agreement/understanding between the detenu and the complainants is illegal.
The complainants cannot offer huge amount to the detenu to get permanent jobs and that they cannot enter into agreements.
The said contract itself is illegal.
However, Courts below granted bail to the detenu in all the aforesaid crimes.
Criminal Law was set on motion and all the aforesaid five (05) crimes were registered.
In the aforesaid crimes, the Investigating Officers have already completed investigation and laid charge sheet filed against the detenu.
In some of the cases, C.C. numbers are pending.

10. With regard to Crime No.77 of 2023, Crime No.82 of 2023, both registered on 10.03.2023 and Crime No.86 of 2023 registered on KL,J & PSS,J 20.02.2023, which were referred but not relied by the detaining authority, the Investigating Officers completed investigation and laid charge sheets.
The allegations leveled against the detenu are different.
11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration1 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.

12. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar2, the Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other .
(1966) 1 SCR 709 KL,J & PSS,J examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.

A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of Smt. Bokka Mallika, vs The State Of Telangana on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119205019/
3 public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

entities.text: Smt. Bokka Mallika, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.

It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."
13.

In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar3, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not characterize as an act of 'habitual'.

entities.text: Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court was of the . (1984) 3 SCC 14 KL,J & PSS,J opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.

14. There is no quarrel that the detention order can be passed based on a solitary incident where the impact of the act of the detenu affected the community and led to disturbance of the current life of the community so as to amount to a disturbance of public order.
But, at the same time, Detaining Authority has to consider the nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed, whether it disturbed the public order or not.
Detention order cannot be passed in a routine and mechanical manner.
In the case on hand, there is no material to show that the acts of the detenu caused disturbance of public order.
Therefore, the facts in the aforesaid decision are distinguishable on facts and circumstances of the present case.
In the present case, there is no material before the detaining authority to arrive at subjective satisfaction for invoking Section - 3 of the Act, 1986 and issuing detention order.
KL,J & PSS,J 15.
The Apex Court as well as this Court time and again held that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order".
The offences which are committed against a particular individual fall within the ambit of "law and order".
It is only when the public at large is adversely affected by the criminal activities of a person, the conduct of a person is said to disturb "the public order".
Moreover, individual cases can be dealt with by the criminal justice system.
Therefore, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the provisions of the Act, 1986 for passing order of detention against an individual.
Invoking of such law adversely affects the fundamental right of personal liberty which is guaranteed and protected by Article - 21 of the Constitution of India.
16. As discussed above, criminal law was set on motion and the detenu obtained bail in all the aforesaid crimes relied upon by the detaining authority while passing detention order.

However, the Investigating Officers have not filed applications seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu Smt. Bokka Mallika, vs The State Of Telangana on 11 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119205019/
4 in the aforesaid crimes on the ground that he has committed similar offences and that he has violated the conditions imposed by the Courts below while granting bail.

sentences.text: The Apex Court and this Court time and again held that the detention KL,J & PSS,J orders shall be passed in rarest of rare cases and to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences which may disturb the public order.

17. In view of the aforesaid discussion, there is no consideration of the aforesaid aspects and the principle laid down by the Apex Court and the Division Benches of this Court in the aforesaid order of detention passed by respondent No.3 and confirmed by respondent No.1.

Therefore, the respondents are not justified in passing the order of detention and confirming the same and,
therefore, the same are liable to be set aside.

18. The present Writ Petition is allowed and the impugned detention order dated 21.04.2023 passed by respondent No.3 and confirmed by respondent No.1 vide G.O.Rt. No.823, General Administration (Special Law & Order) Department, dated 06.06.2023, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the Detenu, namely, i.e., Bokka Praveen S/o Prabhakar @ Cheralu,
who is no detained in Central Prison, Cherlapally, Medchal - Malkajgiri District, free forthwith if he is no longer required in any other criminal cases.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
KL,J & PSS,J
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.
